title: Rank-one Thom isomorphism
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $\pi:E\to B$ be a
vector bundle of constant
rank one, with the zero section $z:B\hookrightarrow E$. The zero
section is an effective Cartier divisor of $E$ (the zero scheme of the
tautological section of $\pi^*E$); let

$$
\operatorname{thom}(E):z_*\Lambda_B\longrightarrow\Lambda_E(1)[2]
$$

be its class $\operatorname{cl}_{z(B)}$ of [lem-pur-divisor-class],
and put

$$
\tau_E:=
R\pi_!\operatorname{thom}(E):
\Lambda_B\longrightarrow R\pi_!\Lambda_E(1)[2].
$$

Then $\tau_E$ is an isomorphism, compatible with base change. Its
inverse $\operatorname{tr}_\pi$ is the *rank-one vector-bundle
trace*. In particular

$$
R\pi_!\Lambda_E\;\cong\;\Lambda_B(-1)[-2].
$$

proof.text: In the datum [def-pur-conventions], use $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\underline\Lambda$ [det-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and the twist notation [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. The bundle and zero section are [def-pur-vector-bundle-zero-section]. By [lem-pur-line-zero-geometry], the morphism has the separated finite-type properties of [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and the zero divisor stays Cartier after base change. The canonical class of [lem-pur-divisor-class] is frame-independent [lem-pur-frame-independence]. Apply [lem-pur-condensed-cartier-compact-exchange] with $f=\pi,i=z$: the compact source is canonically $\Lambda_B$ and its map is precisely $\tau_E$.

For a geometric point $b$, [lem-pur-condensed-cartier-compact-exchange] identifies $Lb^*\tau_E$ with the compact image of the origin class after a basis of the fibre line. At $A_n$ retain the morphism's witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. The local calculation [thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation] makes $\partial\kappa(t)$ a basis of the sole supported cohomology group, in degree two. Pulling back along the fibre, the local formula of [lem-pur-divisor-class] (naturality of the Kummer boundary) makes the restricted class the signed multiple $\pm\partial\kappa(t)$ of this basis, with the sign stated there, again a basis, the sign being a unit at every coefficient. The derived comparison [lem-pur-affine-origin-support-compact-comparison] therefore makes the compact image an isomorphism. Its compatible derived limits and scalar extensions, with the source identifications stated there, give the same conclusion for $R,F,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, in the pulled-back condensed categories.

The cone is bounded constructible by [lem-pur-condensed-constructible-point-detection]; its geometric inverse images vanish by Step 2. The same lemma and the cohomology-sheaf convention [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] give a zero cone, hence $\tau_E$ is invertible. The exchange identity of [lem-pur-condensed-cartier-compact-exchange] proves base change; invert it to obtain the trace $\operatorname{tr}_\pi$.

On the pro-etale ringed sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], twists are invertible modules [sk-def-sp-tate-twist]. With the ring-sheaf tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] (finite notation [def-weil-derived-tensor]) and Tate pullback [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], apply [lem-sbc-ringed-site-perfect-projection-formula] to the proper factor of a compactification and [lem-sfb-open-immersion-derived-tensor-projection] to its open factor. For the base twist line this gives $R\pi_!\Lambda_E(1)[2]\cong(R\pi_!\Lambda_E)(1)[2]$. Tensor the proved isomorphism with $\Lambda_B(-1)[-2]$; evaluation cancels the line and shift, giving the asserted formula.
